title.en: Firefighters struggle to contain Madrid wildfires, as more than 140,000 evacuated in France and Spain
title.zh: 马德里野火肆虐，法国和西班牙超过14万人被疏散

summary.en: Authorities in Madrid describe the ongoing wildfires as the "worst fire in the history of the region," while French firefighters are battling a blaze advancing towards Bordeaux, leading to the evacuation of over 140,000 people across France and Spain.
summary.zh: 马德里当局称正在发生的野火是“该地区历史上最严重的火灾”，同时法国消防员正在努力扑灭向波尔多蔓延的火势，导致法国和西班牙两国超过14万人被疏散。

body.en:
A wildfire near Madrid is "beyond the capacity" of firefighters to contain, Spanish officials have warned, after three fires west of the capital merged into a single blaze.

Spain's government has declared a national emergency after blazes spun out of control in several areas close to Madrid, prompting the evacuation of at least 30,000 people.

Madrid's regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described it as the "worst fire in the history of the region", with the area facing a "perfect storm" of high temperatures, relentless wind and merging fire fronts.

Meanwhile, more than 110,000 people have been evacuated in south-west France after wildfires tore through the Gironde and Landes regions.

The fire changed direction later on Friday and was heading towards Bordeaux, with further evacuations expected. French President Emmanuel Macron has mobilised the military to assist the response.

In Spain, local emergency services said wildfires were moving towards the municipalities of Robledo de Chavela and Fresnedillas de la Olivia, around 50km (31 miles) from the capital.

"The wildfire is at its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain," Carlos Novillo, the Madrid regional government's emergency management chief, told reporters.

"It's not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken," he added.

The Military Emergency Unit (UME) has been deployed to try to halt the advance of the flames, with its main focus protecting areas near the town of El Escorial.

Authorities are also monitoring a separate wildfire in nearby Ávila province, where officials fear the huge Burgohondo blaze could merge with the Madrid fire.

Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said authorities were doing "everything we can" to prevent the two merging.

More than 60,000 people have been affected in the Madrid region, with 30,000 forced to evacuate and 20,000 placed under lockdown, authorities said.

Francisco Martín, the government delegate in Madrid, warned those numbers could rise as "embers are flying for miles and the fire is jumping great distances".

The mayor of El Tiemblo, one of the affected areas in Ávila, said flames spread from Navaluenga to the Iruelas Valley - a distance of about 20km (12 miles) - in less than half an hour. "It was horrific," Arturo Varas González told laSexta.

At least 6,000 hectares of land have burned in the Madrid region, while the Ávila blaze has consumed almost 9,000 hectares, according to officials.

Eight municipalities have been evacuated, including Chapinería, Navas del Rey, Colmenar del Arroyo, Fresnedillas de la Oliva, Robledo de Chavela, Aldea del Fresno, Navalagamella and Zarzalejo.

reflection.en: The devastating wildfires in Spain and France remind us of the profound vulnerability of creation and the deep impact of such events on communities. As Yahweh's creation groans under the weight of these disasters, we are called to compassion for those displaced and to a renewed sense of stewardship for our fragile world.
reflection.zh: 西班牙和法国毁灭性的野火提醒我们，受造物是如此脆弱，此类事件对社区造成了深远的影响。当雅伟的受造物在这些灾难的重压下呻吟时，我们被呼召对那些流离失所的人怀有怜悯，并对我们脆弱的世界重新燃起管家意识。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: ICC top prosecutor removed over sexual misconduct allegations
title.zh: 国际刑事法院首席检察官因性行为不端指控被免职

summary.en: Karim Khan, the top prosecutor for the International Criminal Court, has been removed from his position following allegations of sexual misconduct. He denies claims of an improper sexual relationship with a junior staff member and attempting to prevent her complaint.
summary.zh: 国际刑事法院首席检察官卡里姆·汗因性行为不端指控被免职。他否认与一名初级法院工作人员存在不正当性关系，并试图阻止对方提出投诉的指控。

body.en:
Members of the International Criminal Court (ICC) have voted to dismiss Karim Khan as chief prosecutor for alleged sexual misconduct.

Elected the ICC's third prosecutor in 2021, Khan was suspended last month. The decision to remove him was passed with 82 votes in favour.

The court's oversight body found in June he had committed a "serious breach of duty and serious misconduct" by engaging in an improper sexual relationship with a junior ICC staff member and seeking to stop her pursuing her complaint.

Khan has repeatedly denied all the allegations against him. His lawyer said he would challenge "the lawfulness and fairness of the decision through all available legal mechanisms".

It was not immediately clear what legal avenues remained open to the ousted prosecutor.

In a statement after the vote, the ICC "took note" of the decision of the Special Session of the Assembly of States Parties - the 125 member states which voted to remove Khan.

"The Court will continue to attach the utmost importance to maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful working environment for all personnel," the ICC statement said.

The entire process, however, goes beyond the fate of a single prosecutor and could reshape the world's only permanent war‑crimes tribunal.

The misconduct investigation has put the institution under a glaring spotlight, intensified divisions inside it and played out alongside an unprecedented campaign to weaken, and in fact dismantle, the ICC in its entirety.

The fear among its supporters is that the court will emerge weakened and less able to face the gravest global threats.

Khan, a prominent British lawyer, has been on voluntary leave to fight the allegations since May 2025. He remains suspended from practising law in the UK, after the Bar Standards Board imposed an interim ban while it conducts its own inquiry.

He was unable to attend the vote, held in the United Nations headquarters in New York, because he is barred from entering the United States under sanctions imposed by the Trump administration over the ICC's investigation into alleged war crimes by Israeli officials in Gaza.

The decision follows a highly sensitive process that has left the court under intense scrutiny.

In May 2024, allegations that Khan had engaged in sexual misconduct involving a female staff member were reported to the ICC by a third party.

The court's Independent Oversight Mechanism (IOM) opened an investigation, but the case was later closed after the alleged victim declined to participate.

Critics of the process argued that the investigation had been mishandled, undermining confidence in the IOM.

Investigators ultimately said there was insufficient evidence to substantiate the allegations.

body.zh: 国际刑事法院（ICC）成员投票决定解除卡里姆·汗首席检察官的职务，因为他涉嫌性行为不端。 汗于 2021 年当选国际刑事法院第三位检察官，上个月被停职。罢免他的决定以 82 票赞成获得通过。 法院的监督机构于六月发现，他与国际刑事法院的一名初级工作人员发生不正当的性关系，并试图阻止她提出申诉，从而犯下了“严重失职和严重不当行为”。 他的律师称对他的停职是“非法的、程序上不公平且没有证据支持的”。 这一过程超越了单一检察官的命运，可能重塑世界上唯一的常设战争罪法庭。 不当行为调查使该机构受到了耀眼的关注，加剧了其内部分歧，并引发了一场史无前例的削弱甚至解散国际刑事法院的运动。 其支持者担心法院将被削弱，并且无法应对最严重的全球威胁。 汗是一位著名的英国律师，自 2025 年 5 月以来一直自愿休假，以应对这些指控。在律师标准委员会在进行自己的调查时实施临时禁令后，他在英国的律师执业资格仍被暂停。 他无法参加在纽约联合国总部举行的投票，因为特朗普政府因国际刑事法院对以色列官员在加沙涉嫌战争罪的调查而实施制裁，他被禁止进入美国。 该决定遵循高度敏感的程序，使法院受到严格审查。 2024 年 5 月，第三方向国际刑事法院报告了有关汗涉及一名女性工作人员的不当性行为的指控。 法院的独立监督机制（IOM）展开了调查，但由于所谓的受害者拒绝参与，该案后来结案。 对该过程的批评者认为，调查处理不当，削弱了人们对国际移民组织的信心。 调查人员最终表示，没有足够的证据证实这些指控。 2024 年 10 月进行了第二次移交。随后，此事被移交给联合国内部监督事务厅 (OIOS)，该办公室对不当性行为和滥用职权的指控进行了更广泛的调查。 该调查从 2024 年 11 月持续到 2025 年 12 月，产生了 5,000 多页的证据和证词。 随后由三名法官组成的小组对监督厅的调查结果进行了审查，该小组的任务是就汗的行为是否构成严重不当行为、较不严重不当行为或不构成不当行为提出建议。 这些指控是在...期间展开的。

title.en: Trump vows to investigate EU over fining of US tech companies
title.zh: 特朗普发誓要调查欧盟对美国科技公司的罚款

summary.en: The US president says fines against Google, as well as Apple, Meta and Amazon, should be "entirely reversed."
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Donald Trump says the US will launch an investigation into the European Union and threatened a fresh tariff over fines handed to some of the biggest American tech companies.

It comes days after the European Commission fined Google €890m ($1bn) for operating in a way that squeezed out competitors to its services.

In a post to Truth Social, which Trump owns, the US president said the EU would pay a "very big price" over how it had treated Google, along with other major US tech companies Apple, Meta, and Amazon, which have also been investigated.

"The United States of America is not a "PIGGYBANK" for Europe, nor will we allow it to be!" he wrote.

Trump said any fines should be "entirely reversed" and that he was initiating a trade investigation of the EU while considering "a substantial TARIFF".

He added that the US would "immediately initiate a 301 investigation" over European regulators' alleged practice of "robbing American companies and, in turn, the American taxpayer".

Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 , external gives The Office of the United States Trade Representative the power to react and investigate trade practices believed to be unfair. The second Trump Administration has launched several such investigations , external since last year.

The tariff threat comes just one day after Trump announced new tariffs on 60 trading partners , including the EU, UK and China, of between 10% and 12.5%.

Trump also last month threatened a 100% import tariff on any European country that introduces a digital services tax on American technology giants, despite many such nations already doing so , external for years.

Major tech companies, including Google, Meta, Apple, and Amazon, have donated millions of dollars to funds behind Trump's campaign and presidency .

José Castañeda, a spokesman for Google, told the BBC the company had "worked hard to comply" with Europe's Digital Markets Act but had "expressed our concerns about the impact of recent EC decisions".

"We appreciate the engagement by the administration and US government," Castañeda added.

In addition to the recent fine against Google, Trump claimed in his post that Apple had received EU fines of $15bn, Meta fines of $3bn, and Amazon fines of $2.5bn.

Representatives of Meta, Apple and Amazon, as well as the European Commission, have been contacted for comment.

Shortly before Trump was elected president in 2024, he said Tim Cook, Apple's chief executive, had called him directly to complain about fines the company had received from European regulators.

The call came not long after Apple lost a long-running dispute over unpaid taxes .

Meta, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, has been fined several times by EU regulators, including for violations of user privacy and competition...
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，美国将对欧盟展开调查，并威胁对美国一些最大科技公司的罚款征收新关税。 几天前，欧盟委员会对谷歌处以 8.9 亿欧元（10 亿美元）的罚款，原因是谷歌的运营方式排挤了其服务的竞争对手。 这位美国总统在特朗普旗下的Truth Social网站上发表的一篇文章中表示，欧盟将为其对待谷歌以及其他美国主要科技公司苹果、Meta和亚马逊的方式付出“非常大的代价”，这些公司也受到了调查。 “美利坚合众国不是欧洲的‘存钱罐’，我们也不会允许这样！”他写道。 特朗普表示，任何罚款都应该“完全撤销”，他正在对欧盟发起贸易调查，同时考虑“大幅关税”。 他补充说，美国将“立即启动301调查”，指控欧洲监管机构“掠夺美国公司，进而掠夺美国纳税人”的行为。 1974 年《贸易法》第 301 条“外部”赋予美国贸易代表办公室做出反应和调查被认为不公平的贸易行为的权力。自去年以来，特朗普第二届政府已启动多项此类外部调查。 就在特朗普宣布对包括欧盟、英国和中国在内的 60 个贸易伙伴征收 10% 至 12.5% 的新关税的一天后，就发出了关税威胁。 特朗普上个月还威胁要对任何对美国科技巨头征收数字服务税的欧洲国家征收 100% 的进口关税，尽管许多此类国家多年来已经这样做了。 包括谷歌、Meta、苹果和亚马逊在内的主要科技公司已向特朗普的竞选和总统任期捐赠了数百万美元。 谷歌发言人何塞·卡斯塔涅达 (José Castañeda) 告诉 BBC，该公司“努力遵守”欧洲数字市场法案，但“表达了我们对欧盟委员会最近决定的影响的担忧”。 “我们感谢政府和美国政府的参与，”卡斯塔涅达补充道。 除了最近对谷歌的罚款外，特朗普还在帖子中声称，苹果还收到了欧盟 150 亿美元的罚款、Meta 30 亿美元的罚款和亚马逊 25 亿美元的罚款。 我们已联系 Meta、苹果和亚马逊以及欧盟委员会的代表征求意见。 特朗普在 2024 年当选总统前不久表示，苹果首席执行官蒂姆·库克曾直接打电话给他，抱怨该公司收到了来自欧洲监管机构的罚款。 苹果公司在一场旷日持久的未缴税款纠纷中败诉后不久就发出了这一电话。 拥有 Facebook、Instagram 和 WhatsApp 的 Meta 已多次被欧盟监管机构罚款，包括侵犯用户隐私和竞争……

title.en: Ten killed in Russian attack on drone exhibition near Kyiv
title.zh: 俄罗斯袭击基辅附近无人机展，造成十人死亡

summary.en: Ten people were killed in a Russian ballistic missile attack on a drone exhibition near Kyiv. The event was attended by prominent members of the Ukrainian defense industry and occurred in the middle of the day.
summary.zh: 在基辅附近举行的一次无人机展览遭到俄罗斯弹道导弹袭击，造成十人死亡。此次活动有乌克兰国防工业的重要成员参加，袭击发生在白天。

body.en:
At least 15 people have been killed in Russian attacks on Ukraine, including 10 dead in ballistic missile strikes on an exhibition near Kyiv showcasing drone technology.

Writing on social media, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said some 100 people had been injured in the daytime attack on the exhibition, attended by prominent members of the defence sector.

Elsewhere, five people were killed in the eastern city of Sloviansk by Russian glide bombs.

And on Friday evening, Zelensky said he had received intelligence that Russia was preparing another massive missile strike which "could happen today" or "within the next 48 hours".

Meanwhile, an overnight Ukrainian strike killed six people and wounded 26 in the Russian city of Kirov, more than 1,000km (600 miles) behind the front line. Ukraine also attacked warehouses of Wildberries - Russia's biggest online retailer.

After the attacks near Kyiv, there were initially fears for the safety of Defence Ministry adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov, also known as Flash, and Lyuba Shypovych, who has been involved in developing technology for the Ukrainian army.

Following the incident, both took to social media to confirm they were unharmed, and Beskrestnov said he had stayed away from the event because of security concerns.

Ukrainian air force spokesman Yuri Ihnat told Ukrainian TV the attack involved three ballistic missiles, only one of which was intercepted.

Russia confirmed the attack. Its Defence Ministry said high-precision long-range weaponry had been used on a site where drones for use in targeting civil sites in Russia were being demonstrated.

It said producers of drones, as well as representatives of Ukraine's drone forces and security services "directly planning and carrying out strikes on Russian territory" were present.

This is at least the third time since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 that an exhibition of this kind has been hit.

There has been widespread outrage that a public event of this kind was being held at all and had, apparently, been widely advertised.

President Zelensky said the incident was being investigated, while Ukraine's prosecutor-general said efforts were under way to establish who decided to hold the event and what safety measures were in place.

The attack came hours after the Ukrainian strikes on a factory in the city of Kirov and warehouses in north-west Russia.

Zelensky said "one of the most important military facilities" in Kirov supplying "components for aircraft and missile equipment" used in strikes against Ukraine had been hit.

Friday's attacks on at least two Wildberries facilities in the St Petersburg area were the latest of several over the past week .

body.zh: 俄罗斯对乌克兰的袭击已造成至少 15 人死亡，其中 10 人因弹道导弹袭击基辅附近一个展示无人机技术的展览而死亡。 乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基在社交媒体上发文称，白天针对展览的袭击造成约 100 人受伤，国防部门的知名人士也出席了袭击。 在其他地方，东部城市斯洛维斯克有五人被俄罗斯滑翔炸弹炸死。 周五晚上，泽连斯基表示，他收到情报称，俄罗斯正在准备另一次大规模导弹袭击，“可能在今天”或“未来 48 小时内”发生。 与此同时，乌克兰夜间的一次空袭在前线后方 1,000 多公里（600 英里）的俄罗斯城市基洛夫造成 6 人死亡、26 人受伤。乌克兰还袭击了俄罗斯最大在线零售商 Wildberry 的仓库。 基辅附近发生袭击事件后，人们最初担心国防部顾问谢尔盖·别斯克列斯特诺夫（又名“闪电侠”）和柳芭·夏波维奇（Lyuba Shypovych）的安全，后者一直参与为乌克兰军队开发技术。 事件发生后，两人都在社交媒体上确认自己没有受伤，贝斯克雷斯诺夫表示，出于安全考虑，他没有参加此次活动。 乌克兰空军发言人尤里·伊纳特告诉乌克兰电视台，这次袭击涉及三枚弹道导弹，但其中只有一枚被拦截。 俄罗斯证实了这起袭击事件。俄罗斯国防部表示，在一个演示用无人机瞄准俄罗斯民用设施的场地上使用了高精度远程武器。 声明称，无人机生产商以及乌克兰无人机部队和安全部门的代表“直接策划和对俄罗斯领土实施袭击”均在场。 自2022年俄罗斯全面入侵以来，这至少是第三次发生此类展览。 人们对举办此类公共活动并显然进行了广泛宣传感到普遍愤怒。 泽连斯基总统表示，事件正在调查中，乌克兰总检察长表示，正在努力确定谁决定举办这一活动以及采取了哪些安全措施。 这次袭击发生在乌克兰袭击基洛夫市的一家工厂和俄罗斯西北部的仓库几小时后。 泽连斯基表示，基洛夫“最重要的军事设施之一”为针对乌克兰的袭击提供“飞机和导弹设备零部件”，遭到袭击。 周五对圣彼得堡地区至少两处 Wildberry 设施的袭击是过去一周发生的几起袭击事件中的最新一起。 此次针对零售商的袭击事件，给大量中小型企业带来了打击……

reflection.en: This tragic attack reminds us of the devastating reality of ongoing conflict and the human cost of war. In the face of such violence, Psalm 46:9 offers a profound hope that Yahweh ultimately makes wars cease, breaking the instruments of destruction. We pray for a day when such prophecies are fully realized, and peace prevails.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，他将对欧盟发起关税调查，以回应对美国科技公司的罚款。他引用了谷歌周四败诉的最新案件以及其他案件。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周五威胁要对欧盟发起关税调查，以回应欧盟对谷歌、苹果、亚马逊和 Meta 等美国科技巨头征收的反竞争罚款和其他处罚。 他特别提到了周四对谷歌处以 8.9 亿欧元（约合 10 亿美元）的最新罚款，原因是谷歌涉嫌对其自己的搜索引擎及其 Play 应用程序给予不公平的优惠。 特朗普发出威胁的几个小时前，他的政府对欧盟和许多其他国家征收了最新的关税，据称原因是没有采取足够措施阻止供应链中使用强迫劳动制造的进口产品。 美国的贸易伙伴和盟友，如欧盟、日本和澳大利亚，对新关税的反应既愤怒又困惑。 特朗普在他的“真相社交”在线平台上发布了一篇长文，发出了这一警告。 “欧盟再次出手，像往常一样，直接瞄准伟大的美国公司！”他写道。 然后，他列出了针对多家科技公司的一系列罚款——或者所谓罚款的累计总额——他错误地声称这些罚款是“毫无理由”且“没有解释”的。 他提到了谷歌最近受到的处罚，并声称这使得他们的罚款总额“超过 180 亿美元！”没有指定时间范围或任何类型的证据。 欧盟法院最近确实维持了对谷歌超过 40 亿美元创纪录的罚款——这一过程已经接受了近八年的审查——这是近年来发生的多起案件中的一个。 特朗普写道：“美利坚合众国不是欧洲的‘存钱罐’，我们也不会允许它成为这样的情况！请让这个事实表明，我们将立即对‘抢劫’美国公司进而掠夺美国纳税人的行为发起301调查。” 301 调查是特朗普赖以征收关税的新手段，此前最高法院宣布他在 2025 年“解放日”征收近乎全球性的关税，超出了他的权力。 所谓调查是指美国在内部证明其认为不公平的贸易行为，从而实施报复性制裁，并指的是1974年贸易法第301条。目前有数十项此类调查正在进行中。 特朗普写道：“欧盟将为这种非法和极不道德的行为付出巨大代价，我一直警告他们这一点。” “处罚将完全撤销，并且......

reflection.en: International relations often involve complex disagreements, and the threat of retaliatory tariffs highlights the challenge of maintaining peace. Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peaceful coexistence with all, as far as it depends on us. In moments of tension, seeking common ground and de-escalation can prevent further division.
reflection.zh: 国际关系常涉及复杂的争议，报复性关税的威胁凸显了维持和平的挑战。雅伟的话语鼓励我们，只要我们能做到，就与所有人和平相处。在紧张时刻，寻求共同点和避免升级可以防止进一步的分裂。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Four Palestinians and two Israelis killed in West Bank shooting
title.zh: 四名巴勒斯坦人和两名以色列人在约旦河西岸枪击事件中丧生

summary.en: Palestinians say villagers came under attack by settlers, while the Israeli military says a Palestinian stole a weapon and opened fire on hikers.
summary.zh: 巴勒斯坦人称村民遭到定居者袭击，而以色列军方则表示一名巴勒斯坦人偷走武器并向徒步旅行者开枪。

body.en:
At least four Palestinians and two Israelis have been killed in a shooting in the occupied West Bank - the deadliest single incident there in months.

There are conflicting accounts of the sequence of events in the northern village of Tal. Palestinians told the BBC that residents confronted Jewish settlers who were attacking them. An eyewitness said soldiers then arrived and started shooting.

Israel's military said it had responded to reports that hikers had been attacked. It said "terrorists stole the weapon" of a security guard and killed him, before being killed by soldiers. The other three killed were members of the same Palestinian family.

There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

Ahmed Zeidan, an eyewitness, told the BBC the latest incident began early in the morning, when locals in Tal rushed to confront about 30 settlers who were attacking Palestinian homes.

A local leader of the ruling Palestinian Authority's Fatah party, Essam Saifi, told Reuters news agency that settlers opened fire before Israeli forces arrived and also started shooting.

It said soldiers had gone to Tal following a report of an attack on Israeli civilians who were hiking in the area - part of which falls in an area of the West Bank under full control of the Palestinian Authority (PA) and the other part under PA administrative control and Israeli security control.

A security guard from a nearby settler outpost had gone to the scene and had his gun snatched by a Palestinian who used it against the Israelis, killing him, the IDF says.

Soldiers then "eliminated the terrorist who executed the terror attack", the IDF added.

He was one of four members of the same family killed "in the exchange of fire", said the head of the army's central command, Maj Gen Avi Bluth.

Two video clips have been widely shared by local media - but not independently verified.

One appears to show a confrontation between Palestinians and Israeli soldiers and armed Israelis dressed in civilian clothes as gunshots are fired and a group of Israeli civilians, including children, watch and heckle. Armed Israelis in civilian clothes then push and kick back two Palestinian men.

The second video shot from a different angle appears to show that both men tried to grab the guns - one of them successfully. There is a chaotic scene and several gunshots can be heard as he appears to fire it and troops also respond.

The IDF has said a 27-year-old soldier "fell during operational activity in the area of ​​the village". The circumstances of his death remain unclear.

body.zh: 至少四名巴勒斯坦人和两名以色列人在被占领的约旦河西岸发生枪击事件，这是几个月来最严重的单起事件。 对于北部塔尔村事件的来龙去脉，存在着相互矛盾的说法。巴勒斯坦人告诉英国广播公司，居民与袭击他们的犹太定居者对峙。一名目击者称，士兵随后赶到并开始射击。 以色列军方表示，已对徒步旅行者遭到袭击的报道做出回应。报道称，“恐怖分子偷走了一名保安的武器”并杀死了他。 后来又说一名士兵也被杀，但没有透露细节。以色列国防军没有解释是谁杀害了其他巴勒斯坦人。 以色列国防军（IDF）表示正在为该地区的一次重大行动做准备，并已取消士兵的休假。 自加沙战争爆发以来，定居者对西岸巴勒斯坦人及其财产的袭击激增，这是由哈马斯领导的 2023 年 10 月 7 日对以色列的袭击引发的。 目击者艾哈迈德·扎伊丹 (Ahmed Zeidan) 告诉 BBC，最新事件发生在清晨，当时塔尔当地人冲向约 30 名袭击巴勒斯坦房屋的定居者。 当地执政党法塔赫党领导人埃萨姆·赛菲 (Essam Saifi) 告诉路透社，定居者在以色列军队抵达之前开枪并开始射击。 他说，遇难者中有两个兄弟和他们的两个堂兄弟。巴勒斯坦官员称，还有其他几名巴勒斯坦人受伤。 报道称，在收到有关在该地区徒步旅行的以色列平民遭到袭击的报告后，士兵们前往塔尔。附近定居点前哨的一名保安赶到现场，一名巴勒斯坦人用枪对付以色列人，抢走了他的枪，导致他死亡。 以色列国防军补充说，士兵们随后“消灭了实施恐怖袭击的恐怖分子”。 后来说，一名 27 岁的士兵“在该村地区的作战活动中摔倒”。他的死亡情况仍不清楚。 巴勒斯坦外交部表示“最强烈地谴责塔尔发生的大屠杀”。 报告称，“定居者恐怖主义的升级是以色列政府和占领军提供保护、政治支持和完全有罪不罚的直接后果”。 报告补充说：“以色列官方的煽动行为继续助长和鼓励这些犯罪行为，创造了一种定居者暴力猖獗且不追究责任的环境。” 一名法新社记者在纳布卢斯西南部的现场表示，已经设置了路障，部队正在搜寻更多嫌疑人。 以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡发誓要“全力打击恐怖分子以及策划和支持恐怖分子的人”。 他召集了保安人员召开紧急会议...

In such moments, it is wise to listen carefully to all perspectives, recognizing that initial narratives may not reveal the full truth. This patient approach helps us seek clarity amidst confusion and avoid hasty...
reflection.zh: 约旦河西岸发生的悲剧性生命损失，因各方说法不一而更显复杂，凸显了理解复杂事件的挑战。在这样的时刻，明智的做法是仔细倾听所有观点，认识到最初的叙述可能并未揭示全部真相。这种耐心的态度帮助我们在困惑中寻求清晰，避免仓促判断。

title.en: US floats AI 'kill switch' to stop rogue AI models
title.zh: 美国推出人工智能“终止开关”以阻止流氓人工智能模型

summary.en: A rogue AI agent has sent a "wake-up call" about the perils of the fast-evolving technology, sparking calls to provide a US government kill switch. But what exactly does that mean, and what are the issues with it?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A rogue AI agent has sent a "wake-up call" about the perils of the fast-evolving technology, sparking calls to provide a US government kill switch. But what exactly does that mean, and what are the issues with it?

Lawmakers in the US have called for an AI kill switch after an Open AI agent in testing went rogue and hacked a tech startup earlier this week.

Congressman Ted Lieu, a Democrat, and Congressman Nathaniel Moran, a Republican, introduced a bill named the "AI Kill Switch Act" on Thursday.

The move came a day after Open AI CEO Sam Altman admitted to a "significant security incident" in which an Open AI agent had escaped its testing environment, reached the internet and broke into tech startup Hugging Face to try to fulfill its task. In other words,  Open AI lost control.

Hugging Face is an open-source repository for sharing AI models used largely by developers and researchers. The company's co-founder, Thomas Wolf, called the incident a "wake-up call” and "very different" from the usual cyberattacks.

"This will be one of the most common types of cyberattacks we see", he told the BBC, adding that most firms are not aware that the "game has changed."

In the wake of the attack there were some unsubstantiated claims that the incident was a PR stunt to raise the profile of Hugging Face. Regardless of the truth of the matter, the incident has brought into even sharper focus the threat posed by AI without clear guardrails .

There are different types and levels of kill switch, according to what's gone wrong. What politicians Lieu and Moran want is to ensure the US Department of Homeland Security has the authority to order a private company to shut down an AI model or tool in an incident like what happened this week, when control is lost.

"It is imperative that these AI systems have kill switches so we can keep this technology from causing catastrophic harm, and that the federal government has the clear authority and process to shut down rogue AI models," said Lieu. 

Rather than a physical switch, this would involve any compromised AI company disabling or throttling a number of technical processes to shut a rogue agent, or program, down.

The US government has generally welcomed AI advances. The Pentagon said earlier this year that the US military is fast becoming an "AI-first fighting force," after signing new and expanded contracts with many of the sector's biggest names. In 2025, the Trump administration launched an"‘AI Action Plan" which he said would "remove red tape and onerous regulation" around AI development.

body.zh: 一名流氓人工智能代理对快速发展的技术的危险发出了“警钟”，引发了要求美国政府提供终止开关的呼声。但这到底意味着什么，有什么问题呢？ 本周早些时候，在测试中的开放人工智能代理失控并入侵了一家科技初创公司后，美国立法者呼吁建立人工智能终止开关。 周四，民主党众议员特德·刘 (Ted Lieu) 和共和党众议员纳撒尼尔·莫兰 (Nathaniel Moran) 提出了一项名为“AI Kill Switch 法案”的法案。 一天前，Open AI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 承认发生了一起“重大安全事件”，其中一名 Open AI 代理逃离了测试环境，访问了互联网并闯入了科技初创公司 Hugging Face，试图完成其任务。换句话说，开放人工智能失去了控制。 Hugging Face 是一个开源存储库，用于共享主要由开发人员和研究人员使用的 AI 模型。该公司联合创始人托马斯·沃尔夫（Thomas Wolf）称该事件为“警钟”，与通常的网络攻击“非常不同”。 他告诉 BBC：“这将是我们看到的最常见的网络攻击类型之一”，并补充说大多数公司并没有意识到“游戏规则已经改变”。 袭击发生后，有一些未经证实的说法称，该事件是一次公关噱头，旨在提高 Hugging Face 的形象。无论事情真相如何，这一事件都让人们更加关注没有明确护栏的人工智能所带来的威胁。 根据出现的问题，终止开关有不同的类型和级别。政客刘和莫兰希望确保美国国土安全部有权在本周发生的失控事件中命令一家私营公司关闭人工智能模型或工具。 “这些人工智能系统必须有终止开关，这样我们才能防止这项技术造成灾难性的伤害，而且联邦政府有明确的权力和程序来关闭流氓人工智能模型，”Lieu 说。 这不是物理开关，而是涉及任何受损的人工智能公司禁用或限制许多技术流程来关闭流氓代理或程序。 美国政府普遍欢迎人工智能的进步。五角大楼今年早些时候表示，在与该领域许多知名企业签署新的和扩大的合同后，美国军队正在迅速成为一支“人工智能优先的战斗部队”。 2025 年，特朗普政府推出了一项“人工智能行动计划”，他表示该计划将“消除围绕人工智能开发的繁文缛节和繁琐的监管”。 亚马逊、谷歌、Meta、微软、OpenAI、Anthropic 和三星等公司已同意在新的人工智能工具和功能发布前向美国当局展示。理论上来说，这...

title.en: Flaming teacakes, bedazzled unicorns: The Commonwealth Games' surprises unpacked
title.zh: 燃烧的茶饼，令人眼花缭乱的独角兽：英联邦运动会的惊喜揭晓

summary.en: Three years after Victoria abandoned hosting the Commonwealth Games, the sporting extravaganza has opened in Glasgow.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Head of the Commonwealth emerging from a time-travelling blue box, unicorns prancing on stage, and fire spurting from an oversized teacake.

Those were the scenes at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Friday morning.

Victoria was initially meant to host the games, but withdrew in 2023 due to soaring costs.

Glasgow, which previously hosted the event in 2014, stepped in to save it — and brought their finest, most-bedazzled unicorns to mark the occasion.

This year's Commonwealth Games is running on a bare-bones budget, arriving at a time when people have questioned their relevance, particularly following the Victorian government's withdrawal.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

But despite the troubles, Friday's ceremony was a party — with scenes that looked like they could have been plucked from vivid dreams.

One of the most unique scenes from Friday morning was the image of King Charles and Queen Camilla emerging from a very large TARDIS — the name for the time machine in the long-running British sci-fi television show, Doctor Who.

Gasps and cheers came from the crowd as the royal couple appeared on a stage that transformed into a magic garden.

Scotland's largest city welcomed able-bodied and para-athletes from 74 competing nations, including a third of Australia's 257-strong team who were part of the procession.

It's not the first time a monarch has appeared at a similar event. For the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics, Queen Elizabeth II appeared to skydive into the stadium alongside Daniel Craig, James Bond-style.

In Glasgow, the UK's new prime minister Andy Burnham was also in attendance, alongside Scotland's First Minister John Swinney and the First Minister of Wales Rhun ap Iorwerth.

The opening ceremony traversed through many facets of Glasgow's history and culture, starting with a day in the life of the industrial city, pictured under its famous Glasgow Central Station clock.

The flashmob soon descended into a bizarre fever dream, where dancing unicorns with traffic cones paid tribute to the city's underground club culture.

For decades, traffic cones have been regularly placed on an equestrian statue of the Duke of Wellington and remain a symbol of Glaswegians' resistance to authority.

The unicorn is both a nod to the playful tradition and the creature being the national animal of Scotland since the 1300s.

body.en:
Wildfires sweeping through parts of Italy, France and Spain on Thursday forced thousands of people to flee blazes fanned by scorching temperatures and strong winds.

Thousands of tourists on France's southern Atlantic coast have been forced out of campsites and holiday homes while Spanish authorities ordered another town near Madrid to evacuate late Thursday because of an out-of-control forest fire.

Three firefighters have been killed as southern Europe endures more severe heat, with temperatures topping 40C in some areas.

The total area of land burnt so far this year in European Union countries is the second largest on record, according to satellite data from the European Forest Fire Information System.

Around Bordeaux, more than 20,000 people — mostly tourists in campsites and holiday lets — have been evacuated since Wednesday, as a fire ravaged a seaside pine forest.

"We're dealing with a very dense stand of closely packed pines," firefighter captain Wilfried Schneider told the Agence France-Presse news agency, describing a fire of "rare" intensity.

"We were on the beach and they told us to go back to the campsite to collect our things," said Belgian tourist Elke Urbain.

"We're not afraid because everyone is taking care of us, but we're sad for the people here."

Skies over Le Porge turned orange as smoke rose from charred and crackling pine trees, while helicopters made repeated runs over evacuated neighbourhoods.

United States President Donald Trump said a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia depends on the kingdom recognising Israel — casting uncertainty over the agreement just the day after it was signed.

Saudi Arabia has long resisted joining the Abraham Accords , under which several Arab states established ties with Israel. The kingdom has long rejected joining the accords in the absence of a pathway toward Palestinian statehood.

The civilian nuclear deal announced on Thursday had appeared to be a major win for the Saudis, especially coming as Trump wages war on Iran in large part over concerns about the country's own atomic program.

But Trump threw a spanner into the works with his post on his Truth Social network saying the Saudi deal "will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords".

The White House said that the Saudis knew the deal was contingent on recognising Israel, although it was not mentioned when the deal was announced.

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said recognition by Saudi Arabia, a regional power and home to Islam's holiest sites, would mark a "historic leap" forward for peace in the Middle East.

Leavitt said she did not know of any calls between Trump and Netanyahu following the announcement of the Saudi agreement.

Should it go through, the deal to establish a civilian nuclear program in Saudi Arabia would generate billions of dollars for US companies, but with Trump's latest announcement, it was unclear whether it would ever see the light of day.

HA Hellyer, a senior associate fellow at the United Kingdom-based think tank the Royal United Services Institute for Defence and Security Studies, said if the US "tries to force normalisation on Riyadh, it's not likely to work out very well".

title.en: The US' $166 billion refund comes with a much bigger cost

summary.en: Trump's willingness to use tariffs to create persistent uncertainty signals a greater economic and legal danger.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An Australian clothing company, Nashie, recently received a six-figure refund from the US government, including 6 per cent interest, for tariffs it had paid on US imports. It’s just one of thousands of businesses reclaiming tariffs imposed on what President Donald Trump called "Liberation Day".

Of the roughly US$166 billion (AU$237 billion) due to be refunded, more than US$85 billion (AU$121 billion) has already been returned to businesses.

But while a US Supreme Court ruling in February reversed the tariffs, much of the economic and political damage, and perhaps some of the Trump administration’s gains, will be hard to undo.

Trump’s April 2025 tariffs relied on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), a 1977 law that lets presidents respond to extraordinary foreign threats — yet never mentions the word "tariff".

On 20 February 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled in a 6-3 decision that IEEPA did not authorise tariffs — under the Constitution, only Congress has the power to impose taxes and duties.

The decision placed an important limit on the president’s power to impose tariffs. But it did not end Trump’s tariff policy, which was, from the beginning, designed to buy time to rewrite US trade relations with the rest of the world.

Trump responded with a temporary 10 per cent global tariff, which expires on 24 July after the statutory 150-day limit.

Trump has also pursued more targeted tariffs under laws dealing with unfair trade practices, national security and anti-slavery claims.

These require investigations into foreign trade practices and lengthy procedures, which slow the process and also create a record that can be scrutinised in court.

The US Trade Representative’s findings on alleged forced labour have prepared the ground for a 12.5 per cent tariff on exports from 54 countries, including Australia, China, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, starting on 24 July 2026.

So while the Supreme Court closed one legal door, the Trump administration was already preparing to walk through another. And it has bought itself yet more time.

The refunds paid out contributed to a US$120 billion (AU$171 billion) federal deficit this June, in sharp contrast to the US$27 billion (AU$38 billion) surplus in June 2025.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

summary.en: A food delivery rider has won China's highest literary award, highlighting a growing trend of laborers engaging in creative writing. body.en: A food delivery rider has won the country’s highest literary award. It is part of a growing trend for writing by labourers The hundreds of millions who have built modern China from the ground up – sweeping its streets, labouring in its factories and ferrying its goods – are often overlooked. But they refuse to go unheard. Last week, a food delivery rider won China’s top literary award . Wang Jibing, 56, first caught attention when a poem about his experiences went viral in 2022. The following year, Hu Anyan’s memoir , I Deliver Parcels in Beijing, became a bestseller. In the early 20th century, Chinese intellectuals sought to capture the harsh realities of working-class lives. But it was under Mao Zedong that the idea of writing by as well as about the masses became reality, with labourers encouraged to take up the pen. In an era when the party tried to govern the language even of diaries and personal letters, the parameters of style and content were strict, and this enthusiasm swiftly diminished after Mao. But workers’ writing has seen a revival in the 21st century. This time, it is bottom-up rather than directed from above. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? title.en: 'Strong concerns': Australia meets with China following ballistic missile test

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

Bringing a partner to Australia has long been a costly and time-consuming process.

As of this month, applicants now face a record application fee of $11,710 — up $2,345 from the previous charge — while many continue to wait well over a year for a decision, leaving couples separated for months and, in some cases, years.

For Sarosh Akram, the increase came just as he was preparing to apply for his wife's offshore partner visa.

"It's made me think harder about how to save enough to lodge the application sooner, so I can start my wait in the Department [of Home Affairs'] queue," the 32-year-old tells SBS News.

Living in Parkes, a town in the central west of NSW, Akram is now exploring ways to cut costs and grow his savings to cover the additional amount required to apply.

Akram says the fee increase has delayed his plans to lodge the application, adding another hurdle before he and his wife can begin the process of reuniting in Australia.

Akram's case highlights a broader debate over Australia's partner visa system, now among the most expensive in the developed world, with applicants facing rising fees and lengthy waits, while the government argues the increases are needed to fund migration system reforms.

Partner visa applications can be lodged through two pathways: offshore for applicants outside Australia and onshore for applicants already in Australia.

Both pathways involve a two-stage process: eligible applicants first receive a temporary partner visa before becoming eligible for permanent residency at a later stage. The full visa application charge (VAC), however, is paid upfront when the combined application is lodged.

According to the Department of Home Affairs' website, the median processing time for offshore partner visa applications is approximately 16 months, meaning half of the applicants receive a decision within that period. Ninety per cent of applicants receive a decision within 27 months. The data was last updated on 26 June 2026.

Those waiting times have become a reality for partner visa sponsors like Ahtesham Altaf.

The 36-year-old lodged his wife's offshore partner visa application in January and has been waiting ever since.

"I applied with the hope that I would get a visa soon, as I was paying quite a higher price compared to other visas, but instead I've been waiting since then," he tells SBS News.

Working as a civil engineer in the regional NSW city of Maitland, Altaf moved to Australia in 2023 as a skilled migrant on a permanent visa.

Chant West head of superannuation investment Mano Mohankumar told the SBS On the Money podcast that while recent performance has been strong, it's unlikely to continue indefinitely.

Strong international sharemarket gains helped drive returns, with global shares rising more than 25 per cent over the year. Australian shares also posted solid gains of around 6 per cent.

One of the few weaker spots was Australian listed property, which comes as new figures from Domain showed national median house and unit prices recorded their first quarterly decline in more than three years.

The chance of another interest rate rise increased this week after stronger-than-expected employment figures.

More than 76,000 jobs were created last month, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.4 per cent because more Australians entered the workforce, pushing the participation rate to a one-year high of 67 per cent.

The participation rate measures the share of working-age Australians who are either employed or actively looking for work. Economists say the increase could reflect ongoing demand for workers or more people seeking employment as cost of living pressures persist.

Citi Australia senior economist Faraz Syed told the SBS On the Money podcast the key concern for the Reserve Bank is whether a tight labour market starts driving wages significantly higher.

The next official inflation figures will be released on Wednesday, ahead of the Reserve Bank's next board meeting on 10 August.

body.en:
The relationship between police and Jewish community security groups came under scrutiny as the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion wrapped up its fifth hearing block in Melbourne.

Across five days, the inquiry heard evidence about the growing financial burden of security for Jewish Australians, police responses to antisemitic incidents, media coverage of the Hamas-Israel war and preparations for future hearings into last year's Bondi terror attack.

Today's hearings focused on the relationship between police and Jewish community security organisations, with Liberal MP Julian Leeser, Dor Foundation chief executive Tahli Blicblau, AFP assistant commissioner Stephen Nutt and Victoria Police assistant commissioner Martin O'Brien among those appearing before the commission.

The evidence is expected to help shape the commission's understanding of police data collection, security risk assessments and the role of emergency preparedness in responding to threats against the Jewish community.

Victoria Police also faced scrutiny over how antisemitic incidents are recorded. The commission heard an abusive phone call to a synagogue, in which the congregation was allegedly described as "genocidal" and "maggot rat Jews", was not recorded as a prejudice-motivated incident.

O'Brien confirmed no incident fact sheet had been logged for the call, which is required for any prejudice-motivated crime that relates to racial, political or ideological circumstances.

O'Brien said the force had "automatic scanning" every day of incidents, along with human analysts to consider threats.

A separate incident involving a 5.5m Nazi hakenkreuz symbol painted on a construction site was also not categorised under the relevant reporting system.

Security funding emerged as one of the dominant themes of the week's hearings, with Jewish community leaders telling the commission families, schools, places of worship and community organisations continue to bear much of the cost of keeping their communities safe.

On Thursday, the commission heard government funding since 2023 has covered about half of the security costs incurred by the Executive Council of Australian Jewry, which received $25 million to distribute to community organisations, places of worship and events.

Executive Council of Australian Jewry co-chief executive Peter Wertheim told the inquiry governments should ideally reimburse the council for all security costs it handles, while almost 200 organisations have applied for the latest federal funding allocation of $124 million over three years.

title.zh: 警方称澳大利亚足球明星在两次超速后检测出可卡因呈阳性

summary.en: Police said Volpato was travelling nearly 50km/h over the speed limit when he was pulled over.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Socceroos star Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine, after police stopped him while speeding over a bridge.

The 22-year-old, who represented Australia at the World Cup , was caught speeding twice overnight, NSW Police said on Friday.

Driving a BMW, Volpato was allegedly clocked at 109 km/h — nearly 50 km/h over the designated speed limit — when police stopped him on Sydney's Anzac Bridge at 1.10am on Friday.

He was subjected to a roadside drug test which allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine, police said in a statement.

Volpato had earlier been stopped at 11.05pm on Thursday, police said, for travelling between 86 and 94km/h in a 60 zone.

Volpato returned a negative result when he was given the initial roadside breath test.

Volpato, who plays club football for Italian side Sassuolo, made three appearances for the Socceroos at the World Cup.

He made headlines shortly before the tournament when he switched his international allegiance from Italy to Australia.

Volpato, who was born and raised in Sydney and played his junior football at Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney before moving overseas, represented Italy at U19 and U20 level.

The 22-year-old, who has scored seven goals in his three seasons with Sassuolo after two seasons with fellow Serie A club Roma, said in March he was "waiting for Italy" to select him for the senior side, who subsequently failed to qualify for the World Cup.

title.en: 'We can't stop this virus': Another state records first suspected bird flu case
title.zh: “我们无法阻止这种病毒”：另一个州记录了首例疑似禽流感病例

summary.en: If confirmed, it will bring Australia's total H5 bird flu case tally to 18.

body.en:
Deadly H5 bird flu appears to have reached Queensland's coastline for the first time as detections in wild seabirds across Australia climb to 17, sparking fresh warnings for vulnerable wildlife.

A deceased petrel found on Moreton Island returned an initial positive result for highly pathogenic H5 avian influenza at the Queensland government's Biosecurity Sciences Laboratory.

Samples have been sent to CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness for confirmatory testing.

Invasive Species Council policy director Carol Booth said the arrival of H5 bird flu in Queensland should alarm anybody concerned about Australia's native animals.

"Bird flu has now reached Queensland's coastline, and that should concern every Australian who cares about our wildlife," Booth said.

"We can't stop this virus, but we can boost the capacity of wildlife to survive and recover from outbreaks."

Australia reported its first case of H5 bird flu on 20 June, and there are now 17 confirmed detections of the serious H5 strain in wild seabirds — 10 in Western Australia, five in South Australia and two in NSW.

Booth said surveillance efforts were working but warned they would not be enough once the virus hit vulnerable species.

"Finding cases is only the first step — once this disease reaches vulnerable wildlife populations, surveillance won't prevent the devastating impacts we've seen overseas," she said.

"Millions of wild birds and marine mammals have died, and unless we do everything we can to strengthen the resilience of at-risk populations, there's every reason to fear Australia could face similar losses."

There have been no detections in poultry and no evidence of large-scale deaths in any animals in Queensland, according to the Department of Primary Industries.

"It is safe to continue to eat chicken meat or eggs, and I would encourage Queenslanders to purchase these products as they normally would," said Queensland's Primary Industries Minister Tony Perrett.

Queensland's Chief Veterinary Officer, Allison Crook, said the suspected positive result was anticipated and the state was well prepared.

"We have known that a H5 bird flu detection in Queensland was a matter of when, not if," Crook said.

"This suspect positive result has not impacted our poultry sector or native wildlife and we are continuing our enhanced passive surveillance program throughout the state and would encourage the community and industry to continue to be vigilant."

Booth continued to urge the federal government to back a major "wildlife resilience" package to help species withstand bird flu and other threats.

title.en: Not just phishing: The scams to watch for if you're an Origin Energy customer
title.zh: 不仅仅是网络钓鱼：如果您是 Origin Energy 客户，需要警惕的诈骗

summary.en: The energy giant has warned customers of potential scam risks after almost five million accounts were affected by a cyber attack.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Nearly five million Australians have been urged to stay vigilant for scams after a cyber attack on Origin Energy saw customer data accessed and disclosed.

Origin — Australia's largest energy retailer, with roughly 4.8 million customer accounts across electricity, gas, LPG and internet services — confirmed that names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and account information were all potentially viewed in the breach.

It said on Thursday it was working to understand how many of its customers were affected.

Also potentially exposed were the last four digits of credit cards and the last three digits of bank accounts.

That combination of data has raised the risk of follow-up scams, particularly phishing attempts that use real account details to appear more convincing.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Phishing scams involve fraudsters posing as a trusted organisation, often via email or text, to trick people into handing over personal details, passwords, or banking information.

But experts warn phishing may not be the only thing customers need to worry about.

New guidance from the company has urged customers to stay alert for scam emails and texts, designed to deceive people into providing their personal details.

"These fake emails often include a corporate logo and look like they've come from a legitimate company," Origin said.

Anyone who believes they've received a scam email is encouraged to report it to Scamwatch .

Origin has recommended customers keep a strong, unique password for their account and never share it with anyone, stressing it will never ask for a password over the phone or via email.

If a scam email arrives, the company's advice is to not click links, open attachments or forward it on, but to report it directly.

To tell a genuine email or text apart from a fake, Origin says to check for a suspicious sender address, spelling mistakes or bad grammar, and where any links actually lead.

"We've seen scam websites posing under originnergy.com.au so look carefully at the website address," Origin said, adding that the only safe way to pay a bill was via their website or the Origin app.

The company has also flagged fake job offers, and bogus calls or emails requesting orders or parts from people posing as Origin procurement staff, as scams to watch for.

Some experts say the breach is another example of a major company failing to handle a data incident well, and are calling for tough accountability standards for essential service providers.
